text: Dr Bryan has been asked to investigate the effects of a new drug for people with a psychological
disorder. Each week, Dr Bryan’s patients visit him to receive the drug and to report their symptoms.
Explain what makes this investigation a longitudinal study.
In the study by Hölzel et al. (mindfulness and brain scans), two participants withdrew from the
sample due to the MRI scan being uncomfortable.
Explain why the withdrawal of these two participants could have reduced the validity of the study.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Outline the most appropriate measure of central tendency to use for a maths test in which
each question is equally difficult.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
In a study, the measures of central tendency from the maths tests of two groups of participants
could be compared.
State the most appropriate type of graph to use for this data.

text: In studies in cognitive psychology, groups of participants are often given tests that produce
numerical data so that the groups can be compared.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest one way that the performance test could have lacked validity. Justify your answer.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Suggest one way that the validity of the performance test could have been improved.

text: In the study by Fagen et al. (elephant learning), one way that data was collected about elephant
learning was the performance test.
Describe quantitative data and qualitative data, using any example(s).

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Jacinda arranges the distance between workstations. In one section of the factory the
distance between the workstations is large, and in another section the distance between the
workstations is small.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Suggest two situational variables that should be controlled so that they are the same for
the two sections of the factory.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
For each of your suggestions in part (a)(i):
Explain why each situational variable would be relevant to Jacinda’s study.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Suggest how Jacinda could obtain a volunteer sample for her study.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Suggest how Jacinda could measure her participants’ interpersonal distance preference,
other than by using an interview.

text: Jacinda, a factory manager, is planning a study about her workers’ interpersonal distance
preferences.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Suggest one ethical reason why it is important that the monkeys are comfortable in the
environment in which they are housed when they are not being tested.
Do not refer to the ethical guideline of ‘housing’.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Suggest one methodological reason why it is important that the monkeys are comfortable
in the environment in which they are tested.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Suggest one way to measure which material the monkeys prefer inside their cages.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Identify two features that are important in the ‘housing’ guideline in relation to animal ethics.
Do not refer to the materials inside an animal’s cage.

text: Dr Foster is conducting research about cognition using monkeys in a laboratory. He wants to
provide ethical housing for them, so will investigate which materials the monkeys prefer to sleep on
inside their cages. The monkeys will be given two choices: leaves or paper.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain why it is better to use a correlation than an experiment for this investigation.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Suggest one way that exercise could be measured in this investigation.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: For the way of measuring exercise you suggested in part (b):

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Suggest one strength of this way of measuring exercise.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Suggest one weakness of this way of measuring exercise.

Section B

text: A psychologist is investigating whether there is relationship between happiness and exercise. He
thinks that either:
• being happier would make people exercise more
• exercising more would make people happier
• happiness and exercise are both affected by another variable.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe how Dr Anand could use structured interviews to study conversations that 8–10 year
old children have with their parents.
Do not describe sample/sampling technique or ethical issues/guidelines in your answer.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Explain how one feature of the procedure you described in part (a) helps to make the
study reliable.
Do not refer to sampling or ethics in your answer.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Explain how one feature of the procedure you described in part (a) could be a problem
for reliability of the study.
Do not refer to sampling or ethics in your answer.

text: Dr Anand is interested in conversations that children aged 8–10 years old have with their parents.
He wants to know about different features of these conversations, such as:
• how long they talk for
• what they talk about
• how positive they feel about talking to each other.
He intends to study these conversations using structured interviews.
